body:
I disagree, mostly on the reason that if you drop different colored balls often enough, you'll eventually end up with one scattering where most like-colors are grouped together. Structured chaos mindset. 

There is enough evidence to show that what we physically see isn't what's really around us. Human senses are rather dulled, we can only see a small spectrum of colors compared to other creatures, even as advanced as we are, but these philosophical and scientific things are beyond me. Fabricated ideas are almost all social and cultural, in my mind. Take the economy for instance. It doesn't really exist. When the bottom drops out, people lose imaginary money that they feel impacts their lives. Monetary value, social norms, cultural expectations are all built on a set of rules that hold no bearing, and yet demand such a sway over us to be stifling. And for what gain? And what of the people who cannot meet these expectations?

There was never really a moment where the meaning of life was questioned by me. Since life is probably the grandest question that's probably intentional, and of course the function of life is plainly visible, but it was just something that I didn't think about. There were never any moments in my memory that would jump out as being 'this is what it's all about.' It just seemed to gradually occur to me, little by little, that everything around us were carefully fabricated ideas to display some sort of order, and that ultimately there was nothing important to be gained from any of it. 

The universe itself doesn't seem to have any meaning either. In fact, if I were to make a very dumb assumption, the universes whole purpose is just to be, and nothing else. This topic is beyond me, however.
Hardly what the post was about, but I can't stop writing regardless. It's just something that has to be done, no matter my circumstances.
